🎛️

Control the app your wayKontrolin ang app sa paraan mo

Use the app without touching the screen: with head movements, your voice, a game controller, a keyboard or one switch.Gamitin ang app nang hindi hinahawakan ang screen: sa galaw ng ulo, sa boses, sa game controller, sa keyboard o sa isang switch.

👁️

Gaze ControlGaze Control

A highlight moves when you turn your head. You choose the highlighted button with a long blink, by keeping still, or with a switch.Gumagalaw ang highlight kapag ibinaling mo ang ulo. Pinipili mo ang naka-highlight na button sa mahabang kurap, sa pananatiling tahimik, o sa switch.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 🦽 MotorPaggalaw
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
People who cannot use their hands or arms well.Mga hindi magamit nang maayos ang kamay o braso.
You needKailangan mo
The Android app (not a browser), the tablet’s front camera, good light on your face, and the tablet in front of you.Ang Android app (hindi browser), front camera ng tablet, maliwanag sa mukha, at nasa harap mo ang tablet.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Open Settings → Accessibility → Gaze Control (Preview).Buksan ang Settings → Accessibility → Gaze Control (Preview).
  2. Turn on Enable Gaze Control. Allow the camera when asked.I-on ang Enable Gaze Control. Payagan ang camera kapag tinanong.
▶See it in actionTingnan kung paano ito gumagana: Gaze ControlGaze ControlVideo 0:24 · PictureVideo 0:24 · Larawan
Open the videoBuksan ang video (0:24)

0:24 · no sound · captions in English and Filipino · uses up to 1.9 MB of data · filmed on app version 1.2.60:24 · walang tunog · may caption sa English at Filipino · gagamit ng hanggang 1.9 MB na data · kinunan sa app version 1.2.6

What you see:Ang makikita mo: Gaze Control is on. Nobody touches the screen: the learner turns their head to move the highlight. Right to the Settings gear, then down, row by row. A long, deliberate blink opens what is lit — here, the word decks. The same head moves work on every screen.Bukas ang Gaze Control. Walang humahawak sa screen: ibinabaling ng mag-aaral ang ulo para ilipat ang highlight. Pakanan hanggang sa Settings, saka pababa, hanay-hanay. Binubuksan ng mahaba at sinadyang pagkurap ang nakailaw — dito, ang mga deck ng salita. Ganoon din ang galaw ng ulo sa bawat screen.

Voice commandsMga voice command

The app listens for short commands and does them.Nakikinig ang app sa maiikling utos at ginagawa ang mga ito.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 🦽 MotorPaggalaw
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
People who cannot use their hands, with or without head movement.Mga hindi magamit ang kamay, may galaw man ng ulo o wala.
You needKailangan mo
The Android app, the microphone, and a fairly quiet room. It uses the tablet’s own free speech recognition; some tablets need the internet for it.Ang Android app, mikropono, at medyo tahimik na lugar. Gumagamit ito ng libreng speech recognition ng tablet; ang ilang tablet ay nangangailangan ng internet.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Under Voice, turn on Voice commands. Allow the microphone when asked.Sa ilalim ng Voice, i-on ang Voice commands. Payagan ang mikropono kapag tinanong.
  2. No head movement? Also turn on “Voice only (camera off)”. The camera stays off and only your voice is used.Walang galaw ng ulo? I-on din ang “Boses lang (nakapatay ang camera)”. Nakapatay ang camera at boses mo lang ang gagamitin.

Game controllerGame controller

First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. In the app: Settings → Accessibility → Game Controller → Enable controller.Sa app: Settings → Accessibility → Game Controller → Enable controller.
  2. Press “Practise the buttons” to learn them.Pindutin ang “Practise the buttons” para matutunan ang mga ito.

Press your switch when the one you want lights up. The camera stays off.Isang switch: Sunod-sunod na umiilaw ang mga button. Pindutin ang switch kapag umilaw ang gusto mo. Nakapatay ang camera.

Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
People who cannot use a touchscreen but can press keys.Mga hindi makagamit ng touchscreen pero nakakapindot ng key. People who can press only one button.Mga isang button lang ang kayang pindutin.
You needKailangan mo
A Bluetooth switch or any button on a game controller.Bluetooth switch o anumang button ng game controller.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Settings → Accessibility → Gaze Control (Preview). Turn on Enable Gaze Control. In “How to choose”, pick “A switch or controller button”. Turn on Scanning mode.Settings → Accessibility → Gaze Control (Preview). I-on ang Enable Gaze Control. Sa “How to choose”, piliin ang “A switch or controller button”. I-on ang Scanning mode.

Pumapasok sa nakailaw na hanay ang isang pindot ng switch; binubuksan ng ikalawa ang Talk Board.

See, hear and read your wayMakita, marinig at mabasa sa paraan mo

Bigger words and stronger colours, words read aloud, Android’s screen reader, and Filipino Sign Language videos.Mas malalaking salita at mas matitingkad na kulay, binabasang mga salita, ang screen reader ng Android, at mga video sa Filipino Sign Language.

🔠

Text size and contrastLaki ng letra at contrast

Font Size (bigger text): Makes all words bigger.Font Size (mas malaking letra): Pinalalaki ang lahat ng salita. High Contrast Mode and Dark Mode: High contrast uses strong colors and thick borders. Dark mode uses a dark background.High Contrast at Dark Mode: Malakas na kulay at makapal na gilid ang High Contrast. Madilim na background ang Dark Mode. Dyslexia-friendly: Uses an easier-to-read font and softer colors.Dyslexia-friendly: Gumagamit ng mas madaling basahing font at malambot na kulay.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 👁️ VisualPaningin
  • 🧠 Cognitive & learningPag-iisip at pagkatuto
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
People with low vision, and anyone who reads more easily with big letters.Mga may mahinang paningin, at sinumang mas madaling makabasa sa malaking letra. People with dyslexia or reading difficulties.Mga may dyslexia o hirap sa pagbasa.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Settings → Accessibility → Font Size. Choose Large or Extra Large.Settings → Accessibility → Font Size. Piliin ang Large o Extra Large.
▶See it in actionTingnan kung paano ito gumagana: Text size and contrastLaki ng letra at contrast4 pictures4 larawan

Read aloud (Text-to-Speech)Basahin nang malakas (Text-to-Speech)

  • 👁️ VisualPaningin
  • 🧠 Cognitive & learningPag-iisip at pagkatuto

People who are blind or have low vision, and people who find reading hard.Mga bulag o may mahinang paningin, at mga nahihirapang magbasa.

The tablet’s sound turned on.Nakabukas ang tunog ng tablet.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Settings → Audio → Text-to-Speech, and Settings → Accessibility → Voice-Guided Navigation. Speech Speed changes how fast it talks.Settings → Audio → Text-to-Speech, at Settings → Accessibility → Voice-Guided Navigation. Binabago ng Speech Speed ang bilis.

🔊

Screen reader (TalkBack)Screen reader (TalkBack)

Hear every button and word with Android’s built-in screen reader.Pakinggan ang bawat button at salita gamit ang screen reader ng Android.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 👁️ VisualPaningin
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
People who are blind or have low vision.Mga bulag o may mahinang paningin.
You needKailangan mo
Android’s TalkBack (free, already on most tablets).Ang TalkBack ng Android (libre, nasa karamihan ng tablet).
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Open the tablet’s Settings → Accessibility → TalkBack.Buksan ang Settings → Accessibility → TalkBack ng tablet.
  2. Turn TalkBack on.I-on ang TalkBack.
▶See it in actionTingnan kung paano ito gumagana: Screen reader (TalkBack)Screen reader (TalkBack)Described in wordsInilalarawan sa salita

TalkBack is heard, not seen, so it is described here instead of shown. Swipe right or left to move from one item to the next. TalkBack reads it. Double-tap anywhere to press the item that was read. Buttons and pictures have names. Filipino words are marked so they can be read in Filipino. While TalkBack is on, the app sends its own spoken messages through TalkBack.Naririnig, hindi nakikita, ang TalkBack, kaya inilalarawan ito rito sa halip na ipakita. Mag-swipe pakanan o pakaliwa para lumipat sa bawat item. Babasahin ito ng TalkBack. Mag-double-tap kahit saan para pindutin ang nabasang item. May pangalan ang mga button at larawan. Minarkahan ang mga salitang Filipino para mabasa sa Filipino. Habang naka-on ang TalkBack, ipinapadaan ng app ang sariling mensahe sa TalkBack.

📘 Step-by-step guideGabay, hakbang-hakbang: Screen reader (TalkBack)Screen reader (TalkBack)

Filipino Sign Language (FSL)Filipino Sign Language (FSL)

Words are always written on the screen. Cards and the FSL Dictionary have Filipino Sign Language videos. Time-up, “nearly time” and break notices appear on the screen, not only as sounds.Laging nakasulat ang mga salita sa screen. May video ng Filipino Sign Language ang cards at ang FSL Dictionary. Lumalabas sa screen ang abiso sa oras at pahinga, hindi lang bilang tunog.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 👂 HearingPandinig
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
People who are Deaf or hard of hearing.Mga Deaf o mahina ang pandinig.
You needKailangan mo
Internet the first time each sign video plays.Internet sa unang pag-play ng bawat video ng senyas.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. Tap FSL on a card to watch the sign. Settings → Fullscreen shows sign videos bigger. Slow-Motion Mode makes signs easier to follow.I-tap ang FSL sa card para makita ang senyas. Pinalalaki ng Settings → Fullscreen ang video. Pinadadali ng Slow-Motion Mode ang pagsunod sa senyas.
▶See it in actionTingnan kung paano ito gumagana: Filipino Sign Language (FSL)Filipino Sign Language (FSL)Video 0:11Video 0:11
Open the videoBuksan ang video (0:11)

0:11 · no sound · captions in English and Filipino · uses up to 3.0 MB of data · filmed on app version 1.2.10:11 · walang tunog · may caption sa English at Filipino · gagamit ng hanggang 3.0 MB na data · kinunan sa app version 1.2.1

What you see:Ang makikita mo: The FSL button plays a Filipino Sign Language video of the word… …with Replay and speed controls, so learners can practise at their own pace.Ang FSL button ay nagpe-play ng video ng salita sa Filipino Sign Language… …may Replay at kontrol sa bilis, para makapagsanay ang mag-aaral sa sarili niyang bilis.

Break remindersPaalala na magpahinga

The reminder never locks the app. The learner chooses “Take a break” or “Keep learning”.Hindi nito nila-lock ang app. Pipili ang mag-aaral ng “Magpahinga” o “Magpatuloy sa pag-aaral”. Tired? Tap “I Need a Break” in a lesson or game. You come back to the same place after.Pagod? I-tap ang “I Need a Break” sa aralin o laro. Babalik ka sa parehong lugar pagkatapos.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 🧠 Cognitive & learningPag-iisip at pagkatuto
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
Learners who need regular rests to stay focused. A teacher or parent chooses how often: every 10 to 60 minutes of learning.Mga mag-aaral na kailangan ng regular na pahinga para manatiling nakatuon. Pinipili ng guro o magulang kung gaano kadalas: bawat 10 hanggang 60 minuto ng pag-aaral.
First stepsMga unang hakbang
  1. In Time limits, turn on “Remind them to take a break”.Sa Time limits, i-on ang “Ipaalala na magpahinga”.
  2. Choose how many minutes of learning come between reminders (10 to 60).Piliin kung ilang minuto ng pag-aaral bago ang bawat paalala (10 hanggang 60).

Learners who need to know what comes next.   1. Routine (My Day): build the day’s steps in order, like School / Class Time, Homework / Study Time, Break Time and Play Time, or your own Custom Activity. Talk BoardTalk Board

Tap picture tiles to build a sentence, and the tablet says it aloud, in English or Filipino. Favourite phrases are kept for next time.I-tap ang mga larawang tile para bumuo ng pangungusap, at bibigkasin ito ng tablet, sa English o Filipino. Naitatabi ang mga paboritong parirala para sa susunod.

Helps:Nakakatulong sa:

  • 👁️ VisualPaningin
  • 👂 HearingPandinig
  • 🦽 MotorPaggalaw
  • 🧠 Cognitive & learningPag-iisip at pagkatuto
Who it helpsSino ang natutulungan
Learners who do not speak yet, or find speaking hard. It changes for each learner: every tile is spoken for learners who cannot see it, a big sentence banner to show others, two big columns for motor needs, and fewer, simpler tiles where that helps.Mga mag-aaral na hindi pa nagsasalita, o nahihirapang magsalita. Nagbabago ito para sa bawat mag-aaral: binibigkas ang bawat tile para sa hindi nakakakita, may malaking banner ng pangungusap para ipakita sa iba, dalawang malalaking hanay para sa may kapansanan sa paggalaw, at mas kaunti at mas simpleng tile kung makakatulong ito.

Open the videoBuksan ang video (0:11)

0:11 · no sound · captions in English and Filipino · uses up to 3.0 MB of data · filmed on app version 1.2.10:11 · walang tunog · may caption sa English at Filipino · gagamit ng hanggang 3.0 MB na data · kinunan sa app version 1.2.1

What you see:Ang makikita mo: The Talk Board helps learners communicate: tap picture tiles to build a sentence, then hear it read aloud. One tap switches the board to Filipino: “Kamusta. Nauuhaw ako.”Tinutulungan ng Talk Board ang mag-aaral na makipag-usap: i-tap ang mga picture tile para bumuo ng pangungusap, saka pakinggan itong binabasa nang malakas. Isang tap lang, nasa Filipino na ang board: “Kamusta. Nauuhaw ako.”
